entries.title: Sky rookie Gabriela Jaquez is finding her 3-point shot
entries.summary: <p>ARLINGTON, Texas — Rookie <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky" target="_blank" >Sky</a> guard <b>Gabriela Jaquez</b> was a solid three-point shooter in college. Through the first nine games of her WNBA career, though, she had never made more than two in a game.</p><p>Then came the Liberty.</p><p>Jaquez made 4 of 5 from three-point range and scored 22 points, nearly helping the Sky pull off an upset. Her secret? Imagining the beach.</p><p>“Me and Rachel [Banham] were talking about how a lot of players, especially me, play better when we’re not thinking too much,” Jaquez said Saturday at shootaround. “So we kinda made a joke where we’re like, ‘Let’s think about vacation, shopping, the beach.’ My mentality going into the game was just to ... have fun and think about vacations.”</p><p>The Sky probably should have tried this sooner.</p><p>They have struggled from deep all season, still shooting only 29% as a team.</p><p>But Jaquez is helping turn things around. The Sky entered Saturday’s game against the Wings shooting 43.5% from three-point range over their previous three games. Guards <b>Skylar Diggins </b>and <b>Sydney Taylor</b> also heated up during the stretch.</p><p>Jaquez is still easing into the three-point shot. She’d attempted only 23 in 10 games entering Saturday, but after her outburst against the Liberty, she was shooting 43.5%.</p><p>That’s a good sign for the No. 5 pick, who already has put together a strong rookie season. Jaquez is averaging 11.1 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.1 steals. Her floor game has translated immediately: She rebounds, runs the floor and finds open seams for cuts. A dependable three-pointer could take her to another level.</p><p>The Liberty performance also snapped a brief lull after Jaquez returned from a hyperextended knee. She played well in her first game back, then followed with three points and five turnovers against the Dream and just six points in an overtime loss to the Fever.</p><p>A trip to the beach — at least mentally — helped her find her rhythm again.</p><p><b>Taylor envy</b></p><p>After scoring 30 points against the Fever and 24 against the Liberty, rookie guard <b>Sydney Taylor </b>has put the rest of the league on notice.</p><p>“Very impressed,” Wings coach <b>Jose Fernandez </b>said of Taylor. “[She] went overseas, worked on her craft, committed to working on her game….She’s really put in the work and she’s getting the rewards of that right now.”</p><p>Fernandez said the Wings considered inviting Taylor to training camp, but she already had committed to the Sky.</p><p>Taylor went undrafted in 2024 and was unfamiliar to many WNBA observers. Not to Fernandez. Before taking the Wings job, he coached at South Florida and noticed Taylor on the midmajor circuit while she played at UMass.</p><p><b>Will the Sky have an All-Star?</b></p><p>The Sky are hosting the All-Star Game in Chicago, but it’s unclear whether any of their players will take part. Center<b> Kamilla Cardoso</b> was their only player among the top 40 in the first returns of fan voting.</p><p>Cardoso is averaging 11.9 points, 8.3 rebounds and 2.6 assists. Her rebounding average ranks among the league’s top 10, and she ranks fifth among centers in assists.</p>
entries.author: Alissa Hirsh

entries.title: Suburban youth football team mourns player fatally shot in Auburn Gresham
entries.summary: <p>A south suburban youth football team is mourning the loss of a former player who was fatally shot Thursday night in Auburn Gresham.</p><p>The 14-year-old boy, who hasn’t been formally identified, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/19/auburn-gresham-shooting" target="_blank" >was shot multiple times around 11:30 p.m.</a> in the 8000 block of South Carpenter Street, Chicago police said. He was treated on scene by paramedics and was taken to University of Chicago Medical Center, where he died.</p><p>The boy was an alumnus of the Midwest Hawks youth football team, which is based in Country Club Hills, according to a statement by the team on social media. </p><p>“There are no words that can truly ease the pain of a loss like this. Today, we grieve alongside a family that has always been a part of the Hawks family,” the team said in a statement.</p><p>The boy’s stepfather coaches the team, according to the statement. He also had four brothers. His mother started a fundraiser to help cover funeral expenses.</p><p>“My baby was so full of life, loving, caring and could make a friend anywhere,” his mother wrote on <a class="Link" href="https://app.99pledges.com/fund/forever14?home_v2=true&fbclid=IwY2xjawSj3kVleHRuA2FlbQIxMABicmlkETFYcWV6ZFYxaW16MVhFVVM1c3J0YwZhcHBfaWQQMjIyMDM5MTc4ODIwMDg5MgABHid3Wh8zlK0h65AXdR246ThRsfoByplHZK7Q_8MCyb9FRRyh_o8PauvhI1H9_aem_YWdncwNJXfyFsWNwFVXZH7OBXky7&brid=YWdncwFHzJezzlechROi-WUhlP0u" target="_blank" ><u>the fundraiser</u></a>. “All I have is memories and pictures left. I don’t have a long paragraph but I know my baby was loved.”</p><p>The team’s statement added that the boy’s mother “has given so much to our program over the years.”</p><p>“To lose a child is a pain no parent should ever have to endure,” the team’s statement continued. “As a Hawks family, we stand beside them in their grief and will continue to support them in the days, weeks, and months ahead.</p><p>“Though his life was taken far too soon, his memory will forever remain a part of the Midwest Hawks family. His smile, his presence, and the impact he made on those around him will never be forgotten.”</p>

entries.title: Kamilla Cardoso finds another gear, but Sky still unravel against Wings
entries.summary: <p>ARLINGTON, Texas — <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky" target="_blank" >Sky</a> center Kamilla Cardoso had been operating at a quiet hum lately: solid, steady, rarely spectacular.</p><p>Entering play Saturday, she hadn’t scored more than 15 points since May 23 against the Lynx. Against the Wings, she reintroduced the higher gear.</p><p>Cardoso led the Sky with 26 points, shooting 10-for-13 from the field, and adding nine rebounds, three assists and two blocks in another game they let slip away.</p><p>The Sky gave up a 14-point lead entering the fourth quarter and lost 93-92, their second consecutive one-point loss. They are knocking on the door but still can’t seem to push through, undone again by small miscues, missed free throws and big calls that went against them late.</p><p>The good news is that Cardoso imposed her will. When she brings force and focus, teams such as the Wings — who are short on frontcourt depth — have no real answer.</p><p>‘‘She’s just a paint presence that you have to worry about,’’ Wings star Paige Bueckers said before the game.</p><p>Wings coach Jose Fernandez was concerned about Cardoso’s size from the jump. He said before the game the key was making contact with her early and keeping her from burying his players in the post.</p><p>Even with that as the plan, Cardoso kept catching the ball where she wanted it: under the basket, deep in the paint, with defenders already in trouble. She drew fouls, finished cleanly or found the open cutter or shooter.</p><p>A physical 6-7 scorer who can see the floor is a serious threat. The rest of the league knows it. The issue is that the Sky haven’t always sustained it.</p><p>They will feed Cardoso consistently for a quarter or a half, only for the offense to drift away from her. Too often, she goes long stretches without touching the ball.</p><p>The Sky know it and are working on fixes.</p><p>One way to keep Cardoso involved through those lulls is the pick-and-roll with Skylar Diggins. Diggins is an excellent pick-and-roll player and has developed quick chemistry with Cardoso in their first year playing together.</p><p>Cardoso said the connection already feels natural. Diggins knows when Cardoso is open on the roll, and Cardoso knows when Diggins has space to pull up.</p><p>‘‘I think that’s been really good for us,’’ Cardoso told the Sun-Times.</p><p>It has, and the Sky can lean into it more.</p><p>The other fix is simpler: Cardoso has to avoid foul trouble so she can stay on the court when the Sky need her most.</p><p>After scoring crucial baskets down the stretch, Cardoso fouled out in the final minute, sending Li Yueru to the free-throw line to put the Wings ahead by one.</p><p>Coach Tyler Marsh defended Cardoso after the game.</p><p>‘‘It was a wrongly called foul on her to put her out the game,’’ Marsh said. ‘‘It’s unfortunate. She played her ass off the entire game to put ourselves in position to have a chance to win it, and to be fouled out on a call that seemed like a phantom call to me, it’s tough.</p><p>‘‘You hurt our players for what they gave. Did we make some mistakes down the stretch? Of course. At the same time, we can’t have those types of calls called on us and then the non-calls go against us.’’</p><p>Some big calls did go against the Sky late. Guard Natasha Cloud was called for a foul on a three-pointer by Bueckers that pulled the Wings within a point. Guard Sydney Taylor also fouled out with less than a minute to go while chasing a screen. She appeared to get hooked on the play.</p><p>Other issues, however, were controllable.</p><p>Free throws were another problem for the Sky down the stretch. They were 19-for-29 from the line, and Cardoso went 6-for-10.</p><p>Late-game execution remains an issue. So does keeping Cardoso available.</p><p>When she plays with force, she is an anchor the Sky can build around. But even her best game in weeks wasn’t enough to put them over the top.</p>
